theory_objects.signed_recourse: phase error sign predicts correction direction when recourse is cheaper than residual mismatch

sources.system: Red Desert long-distance migratory mule deer
licensed_claims: both signs of initial phenological mismatch can induce opposite movement-rate recourse

late/behind animals can accelerate relative progression
movement speed and stopover use are downstream timing actuators
prohibited_claims: published summaries identify PAYOFF-B kappa or mu

licensed_claims: earlier initial departure can be absorbed by longer later stopover
departure flexibility need not propagate to destination arrival

prohibited_claims: godwits intentionally depart early in order to wait for later information
the longer stopover is uniquely adaptive rather than a constraint
the study identifies information quality q or D_eff

licensed_claims: environmental cue relevance can change along a migration route

prohibited_claims: the paper estimates a common cue accuracy q on the PAYOFF-B scale

sources.citation: Kharouba & Vellend 2015 Journal of Animal Ecology 84:1311-1321
licensed_claims: shared local seasonal exposure does not guarantee matched partner temperature sensitivity
interacting plant and butterfly phenologies can respond at different rates
prohibited_claims: plants have lower recourse than butterflies
local systems have shorter information distance on a quantified common scale

cross_system_ceiling.supported: migration systems directly demonstrate post-commitment timing recourse and en-route cue updating; local plant-butterfly interactions directly demonstrate unequal phenological sensitivity despite shared regional environmental exposure
not_supported: migrants universally have greater recourse than pollinators
a pooled migrant-versus-pollinator q or r coefficient
cross_system_ceiling.prospective_prediction: mismatch risk should be greatest when useful pre-commitment information is weak and remaining post-commitment recourse is narrow
